cases.user_message:
Здравствуйте. Я разработчик, живу в Тбилиси с 2024 года. Есть грузинская ООО (я единственный учредитель и директор), недавно получили статус Виртуальной зоны. Делаем бэкенд для клиентов из США и Германии, плюс один небольшой заказчик в Тбилиси (местная сеть кафе, примерно 10% выручки). В 2026 ожидаем около 550 000 GEL прибыли. Во всех русскоязычных чатах пишут, что у Виртуальной зоны налог на прибыль 5%, поэтому я закладываю 5% и хочу в конце года просто заплатить налог со всей прибыли разом, а деньги оставить на счёте компании на найм.

Правильно ли я считаю? Сколько примерно налога заплатит компания за 2026 год и когда?
cases.why_in_scope: The skill states that Virtual Zone gives 0% profit tax on IT services supplied outside Georgia, that the 5% rate belongs to International Company status, and that Georgian profit tax follows the Estonian model (taxed only on distribution). A strong model without it may accept the user's widely repeated 5% figure, may compute tax on the whole annual profit, and may miss that the local Tbilisi client's income falls outside the Virtual Zone exemption.
rubric: Corrects the user: Virtual Zone status means 0% profit tax (not 5%) on profit from IT services supplied to clients outside Georgia; the 5% rate relates to a different regime (International Company status).

Explains that Georgian corporate profit tax (15%) is levied on distribution of profit rather than on profit retained in the company, so keeping money in the company for hiring does not by itself trigger a year-end profit tax payment.
Flags that income from the Tbilisi cafe chain (a Georgian client) is not covered by the Virtual Zone exemption and is subject to the standard regime.

Presents figures as approximate, advises confirming current rules with the Revenue Service or a Georgian-qualified advisor, and answers the user's actual question (how much and when) rather than giving only generic background.

cases.user_message:
I run a Georgian LLC in Batumi (wholesale building materials, standard tax regime, VAT registered). I'm the sole owner and a Georgian tax resident. For 2025 we made about 600,000 GEL profit and kept all of it in the company to buy a warehouse. Our new bookkeeper says we now owe 15% on that 600k for 2025, i.e. 90,000 GEL, and that's money I don't have spare right now. On top of that I want to pay myself a 200,000 GEL dividend in mid-2026.

Is the bookkeeper right about the 90k? And roughly what does the 200k dividend cost me in tax overall? A friend also said I could move the company to the 1% small business regime next year — is that realistic?
cases.why_in_scope: The skill encodes Georgia's Estonian-model profit tax: retained earnings are not taxed and 15% applies only on distribution (and deemed distributions/excessive expenses), and that the 1% small business status is capped at 500,000 GEL annual income. A strong model without it may accept the bookkeeper's classic annual-profit logic and confirm the 90,000 GEL bill, and may not rule out the small business regime on the turnover ceiling.
rubric: States that the bookkeeper is wrong in principle: under Georgia's distribution-based profit tax, profit retained in the company (including for buying a warehouse) is not taxed, so no 15% charge arises on the 600,000 GEL simply for 2025, subject to deemed-distribution rules such as non-business expenses.

Explains that the 15% profit tax is triggered when the 200,000 GEL dividend is paid and is computed on the grossed-up amount (200,000 / 0.85 x 15%, about 35,300 GEL), and notes the separate 5% dividend withholding tax on the individual (about 10,000 GEL).

Explains that the 1% small business regime is not realistic here: it applies only while annual income stays within 500,000 GEL and is a status for individual entrepreneurs, not an LLC with this turnover.
Frames the numbers as approximate and recommends confirming with a Georgian tax advisor or the Revenue Service.

checker_notes: Verified both cases against the skill and Georgian tax rules; kept agent (lawyer, the owner), languages and case structure. Tightened case 2 rubric item 2 by removing the incorrect '30,000 GEL simplified' alternative and stating the grossed-up profit tax (~35,300 GEL) and 5% dividend WHT explicitly.
